question: A line with slope \(2\) intersects a line with slope \(6\) at the point \((40, 30).\) What is the distance between the \(x\)-intercepts of these two lines?
solution:
Both lines rise from their \(x\)-intercepts, where \(y=0\), to the point \((40,30)\). Thus each has a vertical rise of \(30\). Since slope is rise divided by horizontal run, the corresponding runs are
\[
\frac{30}{2}=15\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{30}{6}=5.
\]
Both slopes are positive, so the intercepts lie to the left of \((40,30)\). Their coordinates are
\[
(40-15,0)=(25,0),\qquad (40-5,0)=(35,0).
\]
The two points are on the \(x\)-axis, so their distance is
\[
35-25=\boxed{10},
\]
choice \(\text{(B)}\).
